explanation: Track the previous two prefix counts in uint64_t. Add the one-digit contribution when the final digit is nonzero and the two-digit contribution when its pair lies in 10..26. Unsigned overflow, if reached by intermediate prefixes, computes the recurrence modulo 2^64.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: each digit uses a constant number of fixed-width uint64_t operations.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space for two uint64_t counts and a temporary count.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 C++ algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Every valid decoding ends with either a nonzero single digit or a pair in 10..26, giving disjoint exhaustive predecessor classes. The uint64_t recurrence equals each true prefix count modulo 2^64 because it uses only additions and zeroing. The promised final count lies in signed 32-bit range, so its residue is the exact final answer even if an earlier prefix count overflowed.
walkthrough: For "1213", the valid tokenizations are 1|2|1|3,12|1|3,1|21|3,1|2|13 and 12|13. There are five, so return 5.
edgeCases: A leading zero has no decoding.
Zero can occur only within a valid pair such as 10 or 20.
Each digit must belong to exactly one token.
